component.name: KSipPhone
component.summary: A small SIP phone for KDE Plasma

description.p: KSipPhone is an audio-only SIP softphone that lives in the Plasma system tray. It uses baresip as SIP and media engine and integrates it into the desktop.

ul.li: Incoming calls as KDE notifications with accept and decline
Missed calls with call back from the notification history
Voicemail indicator and one-click mailbox call
LDAP phonebook search with caller name and photo
HD codec indicator, call timer, DTMF keypad, mute and hold
Selectable microphone, speaker and ring device, custom ring tone
Password stored in KWallet, handler for tel: and sip: links

screenshot.caption: Dialer with phonebook search, keypad and voicemail button
Settings: SIP account, audio devices, ring tone and LDAP phonebook

description.p: Feature-complete for a simple SIP phone.

ul.li: Call waiting, do not disturb and a call history
Presence list filled automatically from the LDAP phonebook
Pauses media during calls; media keys and headset buttons answer and hang up
Mute follows the system microphone; push to talk
Window always on top, keyboard and global shortcuts
Call transfer (blind and attended)
Presence list of internal extensions with filter and sorting
Keep-alive for firewalls and NAT
Better search: from the first letter, sorted, name format, icons
Window layout is remembered; extension list can be hidden
Settings in tabs
Contacts from the address book of the computer (KDE, GNOME/Evolution, macOS) after LDAP
Windows/macOS: icons visible in dark mode
Codec selection as a sortable list with checkboxes; L16, AMR-WB and AMR when available
Windows/macOS: settings icon was missing

description.p: Windows: fixes the engine not starting because libre.dll was missing from the installer.
Packages for all platforms and a more portable engine:

ul.li: Installers for Windows and macOS, packages for Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch (AUR), Flatpak and AppImage
baresip is controlled via ctrl_tcp instead of D-Bus
Passwords in the system keychain (QtKeychain)
Single instance via a local socket, new --settings option
Application icon
